newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 9.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Thursday's edition of The Wall Street Journal:
- General Motors received a bid of $9 billion from Raytheon and a somewhat higher bid from Northrop Grumman for the defense operations of its Hughes Electronics subsidiary.

- Brooke Group Ltd's Liggett has offered to turn over sensitive information to states suing the big tobacco companies in an attempt to extricate itself from most of the liability hanging over the industry.
- USAir has asked its pilots union to agree to the creation of a low-cost airline-within-an-airline to compete with Southwest among others.
- AMR Corp's American Airlines pilots rejected a contract that offered only modest pay increases and stock options in exchange for higher productivity.
- ADT said it rejected as "inadequate" a $2.8 billion hostile takeover offer by Western Resources.
- Tandy is expected to report its December same-store sales fell 5 percent from a year ago.
- The Fed moved to make it easier for banks to sell and underwrite securities.
- Consumers bought even more on credit in November than in October.
- Texaco fired one executive and suspended another after an inquiry found documents sought by plaintiffs in a racial bias suit were withheld.
- Bond and stock prices posted early gains but fell sharply in the afternoon.
- Hilton will post a quarterly loss.
- Among 53 stockbrokers arrested for allegedly cheating on licensing exams were two alleged "ringers" and their middleman.
- Fidelity has expanded the group of securities firms that will send their stock research directly to the firm using Internet technology.
- The SEC again delayed implementing new order-handling rules to allow Wall Street time to absorb additional rules expected to be decided soon.
- Treasury securities slumped further as traders reduced bond positions ahead of the release of important economic figures. -- New York Newsdesk 212 859-1610
